mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the tightening signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 70% of triggered instances despite the labor market weakening signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which boosts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of periods with sustained housing starts increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% over two months signals a supply shock, which leads to increased costs and reduced output, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the supply shock signal.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals a shift in consumer spending patterns that boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of periods with RSAFS outpacing GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over a month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the labor market strengthening signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the inflationary pressure signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over two consecutive months signals deflationary pressure, which reduces consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of periods with sustained CPI decline.
